slugify(text) lowercases text, replaces every run of characters that are not ASCII letters or digits with a single hyphen, and removes hyphens from both ends. A letter outside ASCII is not a letter here: a run of them becomes a hyphen like any other run. slugify(text) lowercases text, replaces every run of characters that are not ASCII letters or digits with a single hyphen, and removes hyphens from both ends. A letter outside ASCII is not a letter here: a run of them becomes a hyphen like any other run. Examples are Python. slugify('Hello World') is 'hello-world'. slugify('  A--b  ') is 'a-b'. slugify('x') is 'x'. slugify('!!!') is ''. slugify('café') is 'caf'. slugify('naïve') is 'na-ve'.

The current implementation lowercases text, then replaces every run of non-[a-z0-9] with a single hyphen. But it doesn't strip hyphens from both ends. Also, `text.lower()` on non-ASCII: e.g. 'café' lowercased is 'café', then 'é' is not in [a-z0-9], so it becomes '-': 'caf-'. Then strip hyphens from both ends gives 'caf'. Good.

'naïve' lowercased is 'naïve' → 'na-ve'. Good.

But wait — there's a subtlety: lowercasing can change characters. E.g. 'İ' (Turkish dotted capital I) lowercases to 'i̇' (i + combining dot). But spec says lowercase text first, then replace runs of non-ASCII-alnum. So we follow: lowercase, then replace.

Also, what about characters that lowercase to ASCII? E.g. 'K' (Kelvin sign, U+212A) lowercases to 'k'. Spec says lowercase text, then replace non-ASCII-alnum runs. So 'K' → 'k' → 'k'. That's per spec.

The fix: strip leading/trailing hyphens.

Also note: the regex `[^a-z0-9]` with re.sub replaces each character individually, but consecutive matches each become a hyphen — re.sub replaces each match with '-', so a run of 3 non-alnum chars becomes '---', not '-'. Wait, no: re.sub replaces each non-overlapping match. `[^a-z0-9]` matches single characters, so each character in a run gets replaced by '-', producing multiple hyphens. The spec says "replaces every run ... with a single hyphen". So we need `[^a-z0-9]+`.

Check: slugify('  A--b  ') → lower '  a--b  ' → with `+`: '-a-b-' → strip → 'a-b'. Correct. Without `+`: '--a----b--' → strip → 'a----b'. Wrong.

So fix: `re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', text.lower()).strip('-')`.

Edge: '!!!' → '-' → strip → ''. Good. 'x' → 'x'. Good.

One more consideration: should the regex use re.ASCII flag? `[^a-z0-9]` is already explicit ASCII ranges, so no issue.

Also, what about text that's not a string? Spec doesn't mention. Keep simple.
